samples.summary: DOCX table-cell `w:shd w:fill` is still interpolated unescaped — the sibling of the injection this delta just fixed for run properties
samples.evidence: This delta hardens `buildRunPropertiesXml` so `color`/`backgroundColor` go through `escapeXmlAttr` before landing in `<w:color w:val="…">` / `<w:shd w:fill="…">` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:79,83). The identical sink one level up is left raw: `DocxExporter.tableToXml` does `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')` and emits `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>` with no escaping (docx-exporter.ts:310-311). `CellStyle.backgroundColor` is a plain `string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:441) and is populated verbatim from untrusted import: the DOCX importer sets `result.backgroundColor = '#' + fill` straight from the `w:shd/@w:fill` attribute value (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:171-174), which the XML parser has already entity-decoded. Attack chain: attacker crafts a .docx whose table cell carries `w:fill="a"/><w:p>…"`, a victim imports it (value becomes `#a"/><w:p>…`) and re-exports/shares as .docx; the exporter writes that string into the attribute, closing `w:fill="` and injecting arbitrary attacker-chosen OOXML into `word/document.xml` (and into header1.xml/footer1.xml, which route through the same `blockToXml`→`tableToXml`). Because it is arbitrary element injection into a Word document opened by a third party, it can escalate beyond corruption (e.g. injected field/`w:instrText` constructs), and it also defeats escaping-based expectations set by the diff. `escapeXmlAttr` in docx-style-map.ts:25 is module-private, so the exporter cannot currently reuse it — export it (or route cell fills through a shared helper) and escape at line 311.

samples.summary: Color emitted into OOXML is escaped but never validated as hex, so arbitrary/invalid attribute content still reaches the exported part
samples.evidence: `buildRunPropertiesXml` now escapes, but performs no whitelist: `defaultColorResolver` passes any string through (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:16) and only the first `#` is stripped, so an imported value such as `#ff0000 x` or one containing raw control characters (U+0000–U+0008, illegal in XML 1.0 even escaped) is written into `<w:color w:val>` / `<w:shd w:fill>`. Escaping blocks attribute breakout but not a malformed part that Word flags as needing repair — a low-grade availability/integrity issue for exported documents. The PDF path already validates with `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts:146); applying the same regex here before interpolation makes the OOXML sink defense-in-depth rather than escape-only.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. docx-exporter.ts:309-311 interpolates `cell.style.backgroundColor` (minus the first '#') straight into the double-quoted `w:fill` attribute with no escaping, while the sibling sink in docx-style-map.ts:83-84 was hardened with `escapeXmlAttr` (which is module-private at docx-style-map.ts:25, so the exporter has no shared helper). `CellStyle.backgroundColor` is an unconstrained `string` (types.ts:441) and is populated verbatim from untrusted DOCX import at import/docx-style-map.ts:171-174 (only an `!== 'auto'` check, no hex validation), flowing into the cell at import/docx-importer.ts:427-431; view/clipboard.ts:416-417 gives a second untrusted (HTML paste) feed. No guard, sanitizer, or hex validation exists anywhere on that path, so an imported `w:fill="a"/><...>"` value escapes the attribute on re-export and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into word/document.xml (and header/footer parts via the same blockToXml→tableToXml route). This is unsafe-input/injection, in the security lens, and a clear exploitable weakness rather than a style nit.

finding.summary: Stored color values are interpolated into DOCX XML attributes without escaping, while adjacent attributes in the same element are escaped — an arbitrary color string (which this change confirms can be persisted verbatim) yields OOXML injection in the exported document.
finding.evidence: This change is built on the premise that a non-color string can end up stored as `InlineStyle.color` (e.g. the legacy `color: ""` the diff now guards against at paint time, and `defaultColorResolver` passes any string through verbatim at packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:16). The renderer path is now hardened, but the DOCX export path is not: packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:71-77 does `defaultColorResolver(style.color)` then `parts.push(`<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` and the same for `w:fill`, with no `escapeXmlAttr` — even though the very same function escapes `style.fontFamily` two lines earlier (docx-style-map.ts:53-56, with a comment explicitly warning about attribute injection). Vector: an actor who can write a color value that is not from the fixed palette (a collaborator writing the Yorkie Tree style attribute directly via the docs/slides API, or a crafted imported DOCX/PPTX whose color string survives import) sets e.g. `color = '#000" /><w:rStyle w:val="x'`; on export the string closes the element and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open. I could not confirm an end-to-end write path that bypasses the palette, hence low confidence, but the escaping asymmetry inside one function is concrete.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that the color/fill attributes in `buildRunPropertiesXml` are interpolated "with no escapeXmlAttr", asymmetrically with the escaped fontFamily — is false in this repository. packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:79 emits `<w:color w:val="${escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))}"/>` and :83-84 emits `const fill = escapeXmlAttr(bgHex.replace('#','')); ... w:fill="${fill}"`, using the same escapeXmlAttr helper (:25-32, all five XML attribute escapes, `&` first) that escapes fontFamily at :53-56. The comment at :67-76 documents this exact threat model and states the color is escaped deliberately because defaultColorResolver passes strings through. So the proposed vector (`color = '#000" /><w:rStyle w:val="x'`) is neutralized at the sink: the quote becomes `"` and the angle brackets `<`/`>`, so no element can be closed or OOXML injected. defaultColorResolver at model/color.ts:14-22 does pass any string verbatim, as claimed, but that is upstream of the escape and does not create the vulnerability. Note for the record (not part of this finding, different file/sink): packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311 interpolates `cell.style.backgroundColor` into `w:fill` without escaping — that is a separate location and does not restore the described defect at docx-style-map.ts:71-77.
